chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) walking after the Day of Sacrifice until he pelted the Jamarah, then he returned riding; and I saw him walking after he passed by the Masjid in Mina.
He said, and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nawfaly narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Salih from one of his companions who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) dismounted from his animal slightly above the Masjid in Mina, until he turned to pelt the Jamarah at the spot of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, why did you dismount here?' He said, 'For here is the spot of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the spot of the Banu Hashim, and I love to walk in the encampments of the Banu Hashim.'

key_terms.مَضْرِبِ: The spot/place of striking or standing
key_terms.يَرْمِيَ الْجَمْرَةَ: He pelted the Jamarah (the ritual stoning)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam's location when pelting the Jamarah in Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi illustrates the practical jurisprudence of Hajj, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the permissibility of pelting the Jamarah while riding, yet voluntarily chooses to walk to emulate the Prophet and maintain connection with the Ahl al-Bayt. The specific location mentioned, 'Madrab Ali ibn al-Husayn,' refers to the encampment of Imam Sajjad (AS) in Mina, highlighting the Shia emphasis on honoring the lineage and presence of the Imams during sacred rituals. This practice underscores the spiritual significance of physical proximity to the Imams' historical sites, reinforcing the concept of 'Tawassul' through place and lineage during Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,
‘I saw Abu Ja’farasws walking, after the day of the sacrifice, until heasws pelted the Jamarah. Then heasws left riding; and I saw himasws walking afterwards walking adjoining the Masjid in Mina’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘An Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al-Nowfaly narrated to me, from Al-Hassan Bin Salih, from one of his companions who said:

‘Abu Ja’farasws got down from hisasws animal, higher than the Masjid by a little, until heasws diverted in order to pelt the Jamarah at the spot of Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws’. So I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Why did he get down over there?’ So heasws said: ‘Over there is a spot of Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, and a spot of the Clan of Hashim, and Iasws loved it to walk in the encampments of the Clan of Hashim’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has said the following: “I once saw abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, walking after the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) to throw pebbles on al-Jamar, then return riding and I saw him walking in front of Masjid in Mina’.

He has said that narrated to me Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nawfaliy from al-Hassan ibn Salih from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, disembarked from his stumper a little higher than the Masjid until he moved to throw pebbles on al-Jamar from where Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would throw pebbles on al-Jamar. I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause. Why did you disembark from your stumper at this place?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is the place from where Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, threw pebbles on al-Jamar and so also did banu Hashim and I like to walk in their lodging (descending) places.’”
